title: How I build Daily Dose, a 16-bit roguelike RPG, with Claude Code: rulebooks, skills, a bot that playtests, and pixel art from code
author: Chemical-Sign-203
selftext:
I'm a software engineer and use Claude every day at work. On the side I build Daily Dose, a free 16-bit roguelike RPG, with Claude Code: [dailydoserpg.com](http://dailydoserpg.com)

What it is: pick a tale, draw one of 7 classes, and explore 16-bit places in first person or from above. Turn-based fights where you see the monster's next move, loot you can combine up to three stars, and several endings per tale.

Who does what: I pitch most of the tales, sign off at each step and playtest. Claude writes the code, the art (as code), the music (as code) and the words.

The setup that keeps Claude consistent:  
1. [`CLAUDE.md`](http://CLAUDE.md) holds the rules that matter everywhere. Rules about me (no spoilers, I play the tales too) go in memory.  
2. One rulebook per area (AUTHORING, STORY, ART, VOICE, BALANCE), so Claude reads only what the job needs.  
3. Skills for the jobs I repeat (/daily-dose-new-tale, -art, -copy, -balance, -ship): the same steps every time.  
4. A blueprint for every tale (rooms, locks, secrets, endings), and a test that fails without it.  
5. The engine is a pure function: a run is a seed plus a list of actions. So tests play every tale to the end, a bot plays 400 runs in about 12 seconds to balance it, and the server replays your run before it accepts your score.  
6. When Claude slips, fix the docs, not just the code.  
7. Nothing ships without my yes.

The art and the trailer are made by code too. The long version is in the comments.

Ask me anything about the workflow. Or play a tale and tell me what you think.
